summary: Yaping Dou is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xue Yu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at several Buddhist institutes and the University of Virginia, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and became a professor at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist and historian. He earned his Doctor of Philology from Saint Petersburg State University and held posts at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences, Saint Petersburg State University, and the Kunstkamera (Peter the Great Museum).

Yashaswini Chandra is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Her appointments include roles at Sahapedia (2011–2018), teaching fellowships at SOAS (2011–2012) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (2012–2013), and positions at Ashoka University (2019) and the University of Edinburgh (2023).

Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta. He was long affiliated with Komazawa University, becoming professor emeritus.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD). He served as professor and professor emeritus at the National Museum of Ethnology and held executive posts at NIHU and Sokendai.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and is an emeritus professor at Komazawa University.

Yasuhiro Okazaki is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and has taught at several high schools in Hiroshima.

Yasuhiro Sueki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a short-term study at the Tübingen University Library under George Baumann and served at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He serves as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He held posts at Kyoto University and Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki (1929–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University. He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1974–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He served as a professor emeritus at Kyoto University and held posts at Kindai University and the National Museum of Ethnology.

Yasuko Kojima specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She serves as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yasumasa Sekine is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS, and held academic posts at Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he had a long career there as a researcher, assistant professor, and professor, in addition to an appointment at Nagaoka University of Technology.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology before becoming a professor and dean of letters at Kyoto University, and later joined ZEN University.

Yasuo Goto is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1995–2007) and took up a post at Kyoto University in ~2007.

Yasuo Matsunami (1948–2010) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano and subsequently served there as a lecturer (attested 1992–2006).
